headline: Semis bounced 3.6% on a quiet Monday, but the month is still -25.8% and the next tests (CPI Tuesday, a December Fed hike priced near 80%, CoreWeave earnings) arrive before the damage can be called over.
regime: Semis ETF +3.6% and Nasdaq +1.1% on the day, but -11.2% and -3.4% on five days and -25.8% and -10.8% on the month; VIX eased 9.2% to 23.29 yet is still up 57% on the month. The 10-year is 4.86% with a December Fed hike about 80% priced, so rates are the cap on any rebound. Every AI segment is still down 6-27% on five days; only hyperscalers (-0.1%) held. Power (+10.7%) and neoclouds (+8.8%) led the bounce, which looks like short covering, not new evidence.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: An AI power equipment maker posted a 96% jump in orders, and Powell has record orders (e4bf390297a7, 9109a3369677)
Vistra reported record Q3 earnings and raised 2026 guidance (43f78db3107b)
Power -6.0% and grid -9.5% on five days held up better than chips (digest segments)
Against: voters approved restrictions on new data centres, and Sacks warns the pipeline could dry up on permits (79a1d0264e6e, e82096e52bfa)
Against: AAON fell despite higher profit; Hubbell asks whether pricing holds as capacity catches up (e77c87f3c24d, 3cbded06490d)
theses.change_note: Order and earnings evidence is firm and these segments held best, but the permit threat offsets it, so no change.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: US AI hardware shipments crossed $1 trillion; CoreWeave has a $104bn backlog (550006e5e503, 9175ed6fbe94)
Oppenheimer sees AMD data-centre revenue up 135% in 2027 (56fcaed92bf7)
Astera Labs fell 26% in a week despite record quarterly revenue (e23676c9f24a)
Against: Microsoft is getting pickier about AI data-centre deals (5d8061fc0a52)
theses.change_note: Demand prints keep coming and the price keeps ignoring them; Microsoft's pickiness offsets the backlog, so confidence holds.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Former bitcoin miners lost nearly half their value in a month as money tightens (4d472f45e68c)
CoreWeave options imply a 20.7% earnings swing on Texas politics and debt costs (3eec9d8cadd8)
Cipher cut fair value on Texas risks; Nebius faces permit scrutiny (98bf8ec7cc26, 8bca8b808579)
Against: SpaceX's CFO says new compute pays back in under a year; CoreWeave has $104bn of backlog (751393c90ab1, 9175ed6fbe94)
theses.change_note: The +8.8% bounce changes nothing about funding; CoreWeave's print on Tuesday is the test.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Zacks highlights MU and SNDK as beaten down with rising forecasts (f260067c4461)
Against: memory is -26.5% on five days and -41.3% on the month, the worst segment (digest segments)
Against: Micron halted its Taiwan plant over a labour dispute; Kospi is in a bear market (55ab8e78cd43, f11823fced17)
theses.change_note: -3: no new cycle evidence, a further -26.5% on five days and the Korean bear market; cheapness alone has not stopped the fall.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Sanders: the AI bet is fuelled by $3 trillion of debt and the cash flow numbers are thin (877647b17103)
Microsoft renting less AI compute would help its cash flow (5d8061fc0a52)
Against: hyperscalers -0.1% on five days, Amazon +7.9% (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -4: the group is the only one that held and Microsoft's discipline eases the squeeze; Oracle -11.2% on the month is the exception.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: A Fed hike is about 80% priced for December with CPI on Tuesday; the 10-year is 4.86% (c3351a72bd25)
Citi says sit out global tech until positioning is cleaner; Morgan Stanley expects more downside before a buy (32ad311ae236, 285ae395b7b1)
Against: VIX fell 9.2% and the Nasdaq rose 1.1% (digest tape)
theses.change_note: Strategists agree positioning is not yet clean, and rates are rising again; the one-day bounce does not justify a change.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Voters approved restrictions on new data centres across the US (79a1d0264e6e)
Sacks warns a permitting fight could stall the buildings every chip, cable and cooler needs (e82096e52bfa)
CoreWeave's CEO pledged to pay for power to the Texas governor-elect as backlash grows (522f747fe035)
Against: the power-equipment order jump suggests demand is not affected yet (e4bf390297a7)
theses.change_note: +4: restrictions now have a vote behind them and industry is already making concessions, though no law has passed.

compute.note: Cheap (Nvidia 11.7x forward) but the Huang probe adds headline risk; Marvell -28.1% on five days.

foundry_equipment.note: High margins and growth, -34% on the month, but 2% FCF yields; wait for a floor.

memory_storage.note: Worst segment at -41.3% on the month with a Micron fab halt.

networking_optical.note: Arista +1.1% holds; Lumentum -35.9% and Marvell's deal show the weak spots.

servers.note: Dell -22.6% on five days; no new fundamental news.

power_nuclear.note: Vistra record quarter; only the cash-generating names, not Centrus or NuScale.

grid_electrical.note: Hubbell +1.7% and record orders at Powell; policy fear, not orders, is the drag.

cooling_thermal.note: Trane -2.0% holds; Modine -25.6% shows weaker names break.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Debt and Texas permits; Equinix -0.1% is the only sturdy name.

hyperscalers.note: Held at -0.1%; Amazon +7.9%, Oracle -11.2% on the month.

ai_software.note: -12.6% on five days; ServiceNow -3.0% the best, Datadog -23.9%.

risks: A hot CPI on Tuesday would lock in the December hike and push the 10-year above 5%.
A CoreWeave miss or funding comment could reopen the neocloud and power sell-off.
Concrete data-centre moratoria or permit rules would hit grid, cooling and neocloud orders.
The Nvidia board probe into Huang, with a Nov. 11 congressional deadline, could widen into China export curbs.
Strategists see more downside before a floor, so a retest of last week's lows is plausible.
watch: CoreWeave earnings and any funding or Texas power commentary.
Constellation's Q3 print and guidance, following Vistra's raise.
Whether power and neocloud names hold Monday's bounce.
The Nov. 11 Nvidia deadline and any chip export bill.
